chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali from his father and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from al-Halabi from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a woman who appointed a man as her agent, and she said, 'Marry me to so-and-so.' He said, 'I will not marry you until you testify for me that your affair is in my hand.' So she testified for him. He said at the time of marriage to the one who proposed to her, 'O so-and-so, upon you is such and such.' He said, 'Yes.' He said to the people, 'Bear witness that that is for me and I have married her.' The woman said, 'No, and no honor (exemption), and my affair is not but in my hand, and I did not appoint you my affair except out of shyness from speaking.' He said, 'He is taken from her and his head is struck.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman's marriage agency if she appoints a man out of shyness rather than full authority?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between a woman's mere delegation for convenience versus a full transfer of marital authority (*wilayah*), ruling that if the agent oversteps by claiming full rights without explicit testimony, he forfeits his claim to the dowry and suffers a penalty. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the precision of agency (*wakalah*) in marriage contracts, ensuring the woman's consent and financial rights are not compromised by ambiguous appointments. The incident underscores the practical application of *ijtihad* in distinguishing between social courtesy and legal binding authority in personal status law.
